tool_input.command:
cat > /Users/anhnm/.claude/projects/-Users-anhnm-dev-01-Github-Notebar/memory/prefers-native-over-electron.md <<'EOF'
---
name: prefers-native-over-electron
description: User rejects Electron for always-running/background apps due to RAM growth; prefers native or lightweight runtimes
metadata:
  type: user
---

Anh rejects Electron for always-running or background desktop apps, citing lived
experience with Teams and Claude Desktop becoming sluggish and RAM-heavy over long
sessions. Chose native SwiftUI for [[notebar-project]] despite not knowing Swift.

**Why:** For a resident utility, a permanent runtime memory floor is judged worse
than a temporary language-learning cost. This is product judgment about how an
always-on tool should feel, not a benchmark preference.

**How to apply:** When recommending a desktop stack for anything resident, background,
or "invisible until needed", lead with native or lightweight options and treat
Electron as needing justification. If Electron is genuinely the right call, address
the idle-memory floor explicitly rather than omitting it. Note that Anh's primary
language is TypeScript/Node (no Rust or .NET toolchain installed), so native
recommendations should come with an explicit plan for bounding the unfamiliar surface.
EOF

MEM=/Users/anhnm/.claude/projects/-Users-anhnm-dev-01-Github-Notebar/memory/MEMORY.md
touch "$MEM"
grep -q "prefers-native-over-electron" "$MEM" || echo "- [Prefers native over Electron](prefers-native-over-electron.md) — rejects Electron for always-running apps over RAM growth; TS is their home language" >> "$MEM"
echo "--- memory saved ---"; cat "$MEM"
